title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 23
statement: Points \(A=(6,13)\) and \(B=(12,11)\) lie on a circle \(\omega\) in the plane. Suppose that the tangent lines to \(\omega\) at \(A\) and \(B\) intersect at a point on the \(x\)-axis. What is the area of \(\omega?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(P\) be the intersection point of the two tangents. Since tangent lengths from the same point are equal, \(PA=PB\), so \(P\) lies on the perpendicular bisector of \(\overline{AB}\).

The midpoint of \(A(6,13)\) and \(B(12,11)\) is \((9,12)\), and the slope of \(AB\) is \(-\dfrac13\), so the perpendicular bisector is \(y=3x-15\). Its intersection with the \(x\)-axis is \(P=(5,0)\).

The tangent line through \(P\) and \(A\) has slope \(13\), so the radius to \(A\) has slope \(-\dfrac1{13}\). Intersecting \(y-13=-\dfrac1{13}(x-6)\) with \(y=3x-15\) gives center \(\left(\dfrac{37}{4},\dfrac{51}{4}\right)\).

Thus \(r^2=\left(\dfrac{37}{4}-6\right)^2\) \(+\left(\dfrac{51}{4}-13\right)^2\) \(=\dfrac{85}{8}\), so the area is \(\dfrac{85\pi}{8}\). Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The tangent intersection lies on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\)
The radius to a tangent point is perpendicular to the tangent line
